study type: Experimental animal study (randomized controlled trial in rats)
exposure: Human amniotic mesenchymal stem cells (hAMSCs) transplantation
outcome: Renal function (24-h urinary protein, serum creatinine, urea, kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1))
Renal pathological alterations (degree of basement membrane thickening)
Expression of angiogenesis-regulating factors (ARFs) mRNA and protein
cohort: Seventy-two rats were randomly divided into normal control, diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and hAMSCs transplantation groups, with the DKD groups being type 1 diabetic kidney disease rat models (T1DRM) induced by streptozotocin.
finding: hAMSCs transplantation ameliorated STZ-induced chronic kidney injury in rats by increasing ARFs' expression in kidneys, lowering blood glucose levels, improving renal function, and reducing pathological kidney alterations.
